requirement_text: Minimum setbacks must be provided unless smaller setbacks can maintain privacy and amenity.
Buildings must align with the street and open space systems.
Provide secure cycle parking for residents and visitors.
Buildings must have a high quality appearance and respect local character.
Waste management areas must integrate into the streetscape.
Provide adequate on-site storage for waste and recyclables.
Maximize direct sunlight within buildings and orient windows to the north.
At least 70% of apartments must receive 2 hours of direct sunlight.
Design buildings to minimize overshadowing and loss of solar access.
Specific requirements apply to Residential Apartment Development.
At least 60% of apartments must be naturally cross ventilated.
Maintain solar access to adjacent properties.
Reduced separation may be considered with privacy measures.
Maximize plantings on structures to enhance private open space.
Minimize off-street parking to reduce impacts.
Enhance the overall appearance of Johnston Street, Rose Street, and View Street.
Ensure suitable area for landscaping and deep soil planting.
Car entries should be single width and replace hard paving with landscaping.
Design landscaping for open views and clear pedestrian passage.
Replace hardstand parking with landscaping.
Structures fronting Victoria Road must not exceed 4 storeys.
Height of development must respond to existing and future scale, character, and form of the streetscape.
Maximum ridge height on 170 View Street is RL 14.5.
Adequate access and parking must be provided on and off Victoria Road.
Plantings must provide screening between buildings/dwellings and open space.
Landscaping should represent indigenous species, with formal plantings to foreshore promenade and street system.
Maximum wall height: 4m; maximum building height: 7.5m (two storeys) above Johnston Street.
Development must have bulk and scale that responds to surrounding context.
Building mass and articulation must reflect the character of Johnson Street.
Development must not exceed maximum height in storeys and RL.
Minimum rear setback: 3m at ground floor level.
Building and landscape materials must be fit for purpose, reflect desired character, and be of high specification.
Buildings must have adequate separation to minimize visual bulk and ensure amenity.
Signage must be on non-residential parts of the building.
Buildings should be of contemporary design.
Maximum solid wall length without modulation is 12m.
At least 70% of residential units must receive 2 hours of direct sunlight.
Building and landscape materials must be fit for purpose and of high quality.
Maximize access for people of all abilities.
Development must submit a heritage management document.
Council may require a Conservation Management Plan for significant Heritage Items.
A Landscape Plan of Management/Maintenance Plan must be submitted.
Protect and enhance residential amenity
Built form layout to be consistent with Figure G54
New buildings must not encroach on existing setbacks
Retain and enhance views to and from the water
Parking must not detrimentally affect house presentation
Minimum flexible floor space: 980 m2
Reduce overall building bulk and scale for human scale development
No demolition or cutting into rock faces for parking
Provide setbacks and design measures for future redevelopment of neighboring properties
Minimize adverse impacts of student accommodation on nearby properties.
Minimum parking frontage: 5m
Site specific controls to define desired future character and development principles.
Ensure high resident amenity, safety, and privacy in boarding houses
30% of bedrooms must have private open space of at least 4sqm
Provide communal bathrooms: 1 wash basin and 1 toilet per 10 residents; 1 shower or bath per 10 residents
Buildings must have a high-quality appearance to enhance public domain.
Building design must balance new development with older locality character.
New road must have a total width of 16m and specific dimensions for various elements.
Building design must respond to surrounding industrial character and heritage.
Employment uses must incorporate design and acoustic measures to protect residential amenity.
Site canopy coverage must achieve 15% through landscaping and mature tree planting.
Development applications must include a view analysis identifying private views from neighboring properties.
Minimum Green Building Council rating: 4 stars.
Setbacks must comply with specified details in Figure G12-G19.
A Site Waste Minimisation and Waste Management Plan (SWMMP) must be submitted with the development application.
Waste and recycling storage areas must integrate with Chester Street streetscape.
Building bulk must be modulated according to height, setback, and active frontage controls.
Building height must comply with clause 6.15 of Inner West LEP 2022.
Provide minimum 4 sqm of space for every 500 sqm of non-residential floor space for waste storage.
Provide dedicated space for interim storage of bulky waste; minimum 8 sqm for every 50 rooms.
Ensure high quality appearance of all building facades.
Provide on-site space for storing reusable commercial items near retail or commercial premises.
Provide access to garbage and recycling disposal on each residential level; waste chute advisable for buildings 4 storeys or more.
Provide communal space for recovery of materials; minimum 2 sqm for every 50 rooms.
Submit a Heritage Impact Statement with development applications for redevelopment in the Precinct.
Buildings must have a high quality appearance and consider surrounding character.
Building and landscape materials must be fit for purpose and reflect desired character.
Use heavy materials for base structure and lightweight materials for the top; include screening elements for privacy.
Separation between buildings as per RFDC requirements.
Signage must be appropriate and not cause visual clutter.
Optimize solar access to habitable rooms and private open space.
All development must comply with SEPP 65.
Comply with Part C1.10 for equity of access and mobility.
Maximise access to the development for all abilities.
Signage must comply with Part C1.15 for non-residential purposes.
Buildings and landscape elements must enhance streetscape character and residential amenity.
All development must comply with visual privacy provisions.
New development must follow the lot amalgamation pattern.
Minimum communal open space: 2000sqm.
60% of residential units must be naturally cross ventilated.
Minimum deep soil landscaping: 2000sqm.
Car parking provided at specified rates, maximum 250 spaces.
Achieve architectural design excellence and sympathetic building composition.
Building location and layout must align with Figure 3.
Vehicular access must align with specified locations.
Consider various environmental performance matters in development.
Pursue innovation for sustainable building practices.
Relocate overhead power cables underground with approval.
Minimum building setback from City West Link: 3m
Submit a landscape plan with the Development Application.
Design stormwater drainage system to Council's satisfaction.
Provide a Travel Access Guide approved by Council.
Waste management facilities must be provided within the development.
Building setbacks and separations must comply with Figure G41.
Building height must not exceed maximum in Figure G40.
Minimum setback of 3m from City West Link Road, Lonsdale Street, and Russell Street.
Building design must demonstrate well-considered composition and proportions.
Ensure appropriate separation from adjoining properties as per Figure G41.
Dwellings should be oriented towards Lonsdale and Russell Street.
Ground floor living spaces must face street frontages.
Demonstrate compliance for access provision for people with disabilities in the Development Application.
Landscaping must comply with tree management provisions and achieve a 40% tree canopy target.
Maximum finished floor level for ground floor dwellings: 1.0m above natural ground level.
Car and bicycle parking must comply with parking provisions.
Maintain solar access to adjacent and nearby properties.
Development must maximize principles of ecologically sustainable development.
All development must comply with environmental performance provisions.
Dwellings must comply with BASIX State Environmental Planning Policy.
